references.title: Study to check the role of iron supplementation in helping maintain iron stores in the blood donor
references.original-title: Serial assessment of iron reserves in first time and repeat blood donors, and a comparative evaluation of the role of iron supplementation in maintaining the reserves in blood donors

characteristics.name: Study name
characteristics.value:
Study to check the role of iron supplementation in helping maintain iron stores in the blood donor.

Serial assessment of iron reserves in first time and repeat blood donors, and a comparative evaluation of the role of iron supplementation in maintaining the reserves in blood donors

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value:
A randomised, parallel, participant-blinded, controlled trial; Placebo Controlled

Method of Generating Random Sequence: Computer generated randomization 

Method of Concealment: Pre-numbered or coded identical Containers 

Blinding/Masking: Participant Blinded

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Target recruitment 300

Eligible blood donors aged 18-60 years

Exclusion criteria

1. Participant should not be on hematinic therapy or have iron deficiency. 

2. Participant must not have any allergy to iron formulations. 

3 Participant must not have history suggestive of peptic ulcers, gastro-oesophageal reflux disease, celiac disease, haemorrhoids or any history of occult blood loss every in life time. 

4. Donors reactive for any transfusion transmissible infectious infection (Antibodies to HIV ½, HBsAg, antibodies to HCV, Syphilis and malaria) as per the mandatory testing in compliance with the regulations in India.

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Three arms of study will enroll blood donors and supplement with carbonyl iron with 100 mg elemental iron, and supplement containing iron equivalent to 50 mg elemental iron by oral route for 35 days after each donation and blood donors without any drug/supplement intervention as controls. Therefore 105 days of oral iron supplementation (35 days at one time, 3 courses)

Comparator
Blood donors without any drug/ special dietary intervention - Blood donors parameters prior to first donation will be taken as baseline and then trend of parameters at and after first, second, third and fourth donation will be taken as baseline for comparison with the other two arms where supplementation is used

Treatment arm 1: oral carbonyl Iron (100 mg elemental iron) for 35 days after each of three donations

Treatment arm 2: oral iron (50 mg elemental iron) for 35 days after each of three donations

Treatment arm 3: no drug/ special dietary intervention

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Primary outcomes
Serum ferritin, soluble transferring receptor, hepcidin and C reactive protein 

  1. First Sampling: 5 ml Plain red capped and 5 ml EDTA blood sample at baseline in vacutainer’s at first donation (D1).
  2. Second sample on donation (D2) after (after 35 days of iron supplementation).
  3. Third sample on donation (D3) after (after 35 days of iron supplementation).
  4. Fourth sample on donation (D4) after (after 35 days of iron supplementation).

Secondary outcomes
Serial measurements of the iron reserves will be analysed to find out as to how much role iron supplementation has in preventing the depletion of the body stores in blood donors.

  1. Second sample on donation (D2) after (after 35 days of iron supplementation).
  2. Third sample on donation (D3) after (after 35 days of iron supplementation).
  3. Fourth sample on donation (D4) after (after 35 days of iron supplementation).

references.title: Clinical trial to study the effect of iron supplement ferrous ascorbate on regular blood donors

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value: Registration states they used a random number table to generate sequence.

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Age of donor 18-65 years, Hemoglobin 12.5-16.5 g %, weight more than 45 kg, voluntary blood donor who has donated at least three times, the last donation being within the previous year, and continues to donate regularly at least once per year and other criteria as per NACO guidelines 

Expected sample size 160

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Intervention
80 donors were assigned to receive ferrous ascorbate*

Control
80 donors did not receive any medication

Follow-up 
Weekly follow-up sessions to closely monitor the donors who were administered ferrous ascorbate

*assumed to be taken orally, though not explicitly stated

characteristics.name: Study name
characteristics.value: Ferritin-guided iron supplementation in whole blood donors: optimal dosage, donor response, return and efficacy (FORTE)

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value: Randomised, parallel design, double blind (masking used)

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Target size: 2400-3000

Diseases: Non-anaemic iron deficiency

Inclusion criteria

- The donors must meet all the standard requirements to donate 

- A ferritin measurement must be planned during the next donation 

- The baseline donation must be succesful 

- Ferritin level should be ≤ 30 µg/L

-18years+

Exclusion criteria

- The donor does not master the Dutch language. 

- The donor is currently or has in the last 3 months been taking iron supplements prescribed by their doctor

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
56 days of supplementation with iron or placebo capsules: 

(I) alternate day placebo supplementation, 

(II) daily placebo supplementation, 

(III) alternate day low dose iron supplementation, 

(IV) daily low dose iron supplementation, 

(V) alternate day high dose iron supplementation,  

(VI) daily high dose iron supplementation.

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Primary outcome

The primary outcome is the effects of four different iron supplementation protocols on ferritin and Hb levels and donor health, to placebo in donors with low ferritin levels.

Secondary outcome

The secondary outcome includes the difference in effects between different iron supplementation protocols

Timepoints

Baseline (t=0), first follow-up visit (t=56 days), second follow-visit (t=122 days), final follow-up visit (t=6 months)

references.title: Impact of iron injection on blood donation (FERDOP)

characteristics.name: Study name
characteristics.value: Impact of Iron Injection on Blood Donation (FERDOP)

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value: A parallel, single (participant) blinded, randomised trial

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Blood donors:

  • Males aged between 20 and 35 years
  • BMI between 18 and 30
  • Ferritin < 50ug/l
  • Transferrin saturation < 20 if ferritin between 20 and 50ug/l

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Treatment arm 1: injection of a 250mL saline solution added with 500mg of iron (Ferinject)

Treatment arm 2: injection of a placebo (250mL saline solution)

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value: Serum ferritin level variations due to iron injection or blood donation (primary outcome); Hb level variations due to iron injection or blood donation; reticulocyte% variations due to iron injection or blood donation. Outcomes measured at 8 weeks.

characteristics.name: Study name
characteristics.value: Randomized Open Comparative Trial of Oral Sucrosomial Iron (SiderAl Forte®) and Oral Iron Sulphate (Duroferon®) to Blood Donors.

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value: Randomised, parallel assignment, no masking (open label)

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Enrollment 120

Inclusion criteria
Blood donors at Uppsala University hospital wo have been donating blood regularly the last two years are eligible to participate in the study. 18years+

Exclusion criteria
Donors who cannot be accepted for blood donation anymore because they do not fulfill the Swedish criteria for blood donation.

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Intervention 1: Oral sucrosomial Iron (SiderAl Forte®): 20 capsules of Sucrosomial Iron 30 mg is given after blood donation

Intervention 2: Oral iron sulphate (Duroferon®): 20 tablets of oral iron sulphate (Duroferon®) 100 mg is given after blood donation

characteristics.value: BLOODSAFE- Implementation of Iron Supplementation and Nutritional Counselling Interventions to Improve Availability and Safety of Blood in Ghana-a Type I Pragmatic Effectiveness- Implementation Hybrid Trial

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value: Randomised, parallel design, no masking (open label)

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Expected enrollment 528

Inclusion criteria

  • individuals between 18 - 60 years who weigh at least 50kg
  • pass pre-donation screening using the NBSG standardized donor screening questionnaire
  • vital signs meet the NBSG requirement for blood donation
  • non-contact forehead temperature not exceeding 37.5°C
  • meeting acceptable requirements for skin lesions, needle marks and physical appearance.
  • willingness and ability to consent
  • understands one of English, Twi, Ewe, or Ga
  • deferred for low haemoglobin
  • intend to remain in the study during the entire length of the study

Exclusion criteria

  • persons who have used iron supplementation within the past one month
  • potential donors who are found to have haemoglobin Hb < 10g/dl (females) and Hb<11g/dl (males) at screening

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Dietary supplement: supplementation with low dose elemental iron 65mg daily

Control: standard care

Secondary Proportion who attempt blood donation (12 months)
